answerBody:
The default trigger should be ex ante: obligations should attach when a developer plans or conducts training, modification, or deployment above measurable projected frontier indicators, with observed hazardous capabilities used as an escalation path, a backstop for smaller systems, and a release condition. A capability-only trigger is too late for the risks that justify conditional approval.

The main reason is timing. Before a large run, the developer already knows unusually probative facts: compute budget, architecture class, tool-use and autonomy objectives, security posture, deployment plan, and whether it has the staff and capital to scale post-training scaffolding. The European Union’s AI Act reflects this logic. Article 51 presumes systemic risk above 10^25 training FLOP, while the European Commission’s 2025 guidance says providers can know before completion whether that threshold will be met and that risk assessment obligations can concern development as well as market placement. California’s 2025 Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act similarly uses frontier-model thresholds while requiring large developers to maintain frameworks for catastrophic-risk assessment, mitigation, internal-use risks, incidents, and protected employee reporting. These proxies are imperfect, but they are administrable enough to start oversight before the evidence is locked inside the lab.

A capability-only trigger sounds more scientific: regulate the model that actually demonstrates cyber, bio, deception, autonomous replication, or loss-of-control-relevant abilities, not one that merely consumed many chips. That is the strongest counterargument. Compute thresholds can miss algorithmic breakthroughs, overregulate inefficient training runs, favor incumbents with compliance departments, and invite developers to shard training or relabel post-training work. It would be perverse to delay a costly but harmless model while ignoring a cheaper system made dangerous by scaffolding, tools, or fine-tuning.

But those objections defeat crude compute licensing, not an input-triggered conditional approval regime. Capability tests are not stable enough to be the front door. They can produce false negatives because evaluators lack time, access, elicitation skill, or knowledge of the developer’s planned agentic wrapper. A January 2026 paper by Charnock and coauthors on external access for dangerous-capability evaluations warned that limited model access, limited information, and short evaluation windows reduce evaluation rigor. Some evidence appears only after dangerous affordances are attached; waiting until then can make remedies harder, especially for open-weight release.

The right default is tiered and rebuttable. Crossing objective inputs should trigger notice, documentation, evaluator access planning, cybersecurity requirements, incident reporting, and authority for time-limited pauses. The regulator should update thresholds for hardware and algorithmic efficiency, include developer capacity and intended autonomy, and treat anti-evasion restructuring as covered. Observed hazardous capability should independently trigger the same or higher tier even below scale thresholds, and failed evaluations should determine whether deployment is delayed. Developers should be able to show materially lower risk, but the burden should shift before irreversible release.

Under uncertainty, ex ante scale-plus-intent triggers minimize catastrophic false negatives while preserving a capability-based off-ramp and backstop. Frontier oversight should not wait for the fire alarm to prove the building is already burning.
rationale: The submission chooses an ex ante scale-plus-intent trigger as the governing default, while incorporating observed hazardous capability as an escalation and backstop. It is grounded in current official EU and California frontier-AI frameworks and in recent evaluator-access literature, and it addresses the strongest capability-trigger counterargument. The deadline was checked after research, and the word-counting capability confirmed answerBody is within range.
